title: P1 B.2 high-energy path and opacity interpolation audit

benchmark.opacity_grid_definition: 640 composite Gauss-Legendre nodes over [0,5,8,10,12,15,18,20,22,24,25] km plus endpoints
benchmark.transport_baseline: B.16, fixed omega, scalar polarization-summed opacity, Euclidean chord, Rmax=25 km

direct_s_path_crosscheck.engine: OpenAI Code Mode V8 binary64; calculation executed directly, not through GitHub Actions
direct_s_path_crosscheck.method: Direct Gauss-Legendre integration in path coordinate s, splitting at every 642-node opacity interpolation crossing, every radial shell boundary, and the inward-ray turning point; compared with the analytic radial primitive for the same piecewise-linear opacity table.

angle_average.method: Independent composite Simpson 128/256/512 and Gauss-Legendre 32/64 over cos(theta), with the analytic path primitive
angle_average.note: Four representative (r0,omega) pairs in the 210 and 510 MeV bands; these are local angular checks, not a new global luminosity integration.

profile_vertex_vs_opacity_grid.method: Recompute B.16 local reduced neutrino and Compton opacities on both the 642-node opacity grid and all 1687 retained profile vertices; integrate the piecewise-linear radial opacity exactly along each chord.

local_integrals.muon_susceptibility: Composite Simpson, 1024 momentum intervals, p in [0,1200] MeV

profile_vertex_vs_opacity_grid.interpretation: Retaining every original profile vertex changes the representative-ray total optical depth by at most 1.87e-5 and the sampled angular escape averages by at most 2.18e-5. The 642-node opacity interpolation does not hide a percent-level high-energy propagation effect.

path_redshift_channel_decomposition.method: Direct s integration split at all 1687 profile vertices and shell boundaries; 4-point Gauss-Legendre per segment; 64-point Gauss-Legendre Fermi-pair angular average; susceptibility integrated by composite Simpson with 1024 momentum intervals.
path_redshift_channel_decomposition.statistic: Unweighted descriptive statistics across the 36 selected rays; not source-, energy-, or angle-weighted global averages.
path_redshift_channel_decomposition.interpretation: For the sampled high-energy rays, path redshift changes the neutrino inverse-decay opacity by several percent while leaving the semi-Compton opacity nearly unchanged. This identifies the channel responsible for the previously measured high-energy redshift sensitivity, but does not establish that the unpublished Fig. 7 code used the redshifted prescription.

conclusions: No path quadrature, angle quadrature, or 642-node radial opacity interpolation error capable of explaining the +92.2406% fixed-omega strong-endpoint residual was found in the targeted high-energy B.2 tests.
The 1687-vertex opacity stress test confirms that the current 642-node opacity interpolation is adequate for the sampled high-energy rays.
The path-redshift sensitivity is carried by neutrino inverse-decay opacity; the semi-Compton opacity is effectively unchanged in the sampled high-energy rays.
Fixed-omega remains the literal displayed Eq. (B.2) baseline. The path-redshift branch remains a separate physical sensitivity, not a replacement or empirical correction.
limitations: The 36-ray redshift channel statistics are unweighted diagnostic samples, not global source-weighted averages.
The 60-ray vertex-preserving comparison and 108-ray direct-s check are targeted high-energy diagnostics, not a full re-integration of the 25-point Fig. 7 curve.
The stellar profile is reconstructed from public figures; it is not the original Garching snapshot.
